questions.text: A clustering index is defined on the fields which are of type
questions.solution:
A clustering index is built on the field the file is ordered by, when that field is not a key (many records can share a value). On an ordering key field it would be a primary index.

Answer: non-key and ordering

questions.text: The order of a leaf node in a [latex]B^+[/latex] - tree is the maximum number of (value, data record pointer) pairs it can hold. Given that the block size is 1K bytes, data record pointer is 7 bytes long, the value field is 9 bytes long and a block pointer is 6 bytes long, what is the order of the leaf node?
questions.solution:
A leaf holds n (value, record pointer) pairs plus one block pointer to the next leaf:
[latex]n(9+7)+6\le1024\Rightarrow16n\le1018\Rightarrow n=63[/latex]

Answer: 63

questions.text:
Given the relations
employee (name, salary, dept-no), and
department (dept-no, dept-name,address),
Which of the following queries cannot be expressed using the basic relational algebra operations [latex]\left(\sigma, \pi,\times ,\Join, \cup, \cap,-\right)[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Basic relational algebra (select, project, product, join, set operations) has no aggregation, so it cannot add up salaries. The other queries are joins and selections.

Answer: The sum of all employees' salaries

The sum of all employees' salaries
All employees of a given department
